questions.question: What is the DOM and how do you update it safely?
questions.title: DOM tree and manipulation
questions.direct_answer: The DOM is the browser's object representation of an HTML document. Select the smallest required element, update text or classes with DOM APIs, and use event delegation for repeated children instead of rebuilding the whole page.

interviewer_intent.testing: Browser fundamentals and safe UI updates.
interviewer_intent.common_mistake: Using innerHTML with untrusted data or querying the document repeatedly in a loop.
interviewer_intent.to_stand_out: Distinguish textContent from innerHTML and mention batching reads and writes.

sections.title: What the interviewer wants
sections.content: Define DOM tree and manipulation simply, show a small example, and mention the main trade-off or edge case.

sections.title: A live document tree
sections.content: The browser parses HTML into nodes. JavaScript can read or change those nodes, and the browser then paints the updated view.

sections.title: Safe habits
items: Use textContent for plain user-provided text.
Delegate events from a stable parent for dynamic lists.

sections.title: Interview answer
sections.content: The DOM is a live tree of document nodes. I update only the affected node, use textContent for untrusted strings, and avoid unnecessary layout work by batching DOM reads and writes.

sections.title: Concept explained
sections.content: Walk through the example step by step, then say when this approach is a good fit and what you would test at the boundary.
